purpose: Normalize the new story-development router contracts so every newly added endpoint in `build_story_development_router()` passes only existing, service-compatible arguments. Scope is limited to `POST /foundation`, `PATCH /foundation`, `PATCH /characters/{character_id}`, `POST /relationships`, `POST /world-bible`, `PATCH /world-bible/{entry_type}/{title}`, `GET /characters/{character_id}/relationships`, `GET /arcs/candidates`, and `GET /arcs/stage-maps`. Do not introduce new endpoint families, new persistence fields, or any non-requested refactor; only reconcile request/response mapping, required field handling, and method invocations so the current backend stops throwing 500s on first FE calls.

route_inputs.POST /story-development/foundation: Must supply the exact fields required by `FoundationProfileInput.from_mapping()`: `premise`, `logline`, `thematic_spine`, `emotional_promise`, `tone_and_voice_direction`, `target_audience`, `narrative_constraints`, `complexity_level`, `success_definition`.
route_inputs.PATCH /story-development/characters/{cha: Must merge only service-supported `CharacterProfile` fields; exclude `relationship_edges` from the upsert payload.
route_inputs.POST /story-development/relationships: Map request fields to `source_character_id`, `target_character_id`, `relation_kind`, `summary`, `tension`, `notes`, and `edge_id` only.
route_inputs.POST/PATCH /story-development/world-bibl: Map request fields to the existing `WorldBibleEntry` contract: `summary`, `canonical_facts`, `related_character_ids`, `source_artifacts`, `visibility_scope`, `continuity_warnings`, `writer_notes`.

response_constraints: Route handlers must return the already-defined schema objects without accessing nonexistent attributes such as `existing.content`, `existing.related_entry_ids`, or `existing.importance_level`.
GET list route metadata must remain internally consistent with the actual service ordering.

utilized_features: FastAPI route handlers already defined in `build_story_development_router`
Existing `HTTPException` 400/404 handling patterns already used in this module
expected_outcomes: `POST /story-development/foundation` no longer raises `TypeError` for missing required service fields; it either succeeds with `FoundationWriteResponse` or returns a controlled 4xx.
`POST /story-development/relationships` invokes `StoryKnowledgeService.upsert_relationship_edge()` with the exact supported keyword arguments.
`POST` and `PATCH` world-bible routes stop dereferencing nonexistent `WorldBibleEntry` attributes and return schema-valid responses.
Router calls to relationship and arc list endpoints reference real service methods only.
No unrelated endpoints, response models, or persistence tables are modified.

purpose: Complete the missing `StoryKnowledgeService` read surface required by the new router by implementing only the absent methods `list_relationship_edges_for_character()`, `list_arc_candidates()`, and `list_arc_stage_maps()`. Keep the implementation as thin projections over existing repository methods and current schema converters; do not redesign ranking, selection, persistence, or decision-record behavior.

parameter_rules: Normalize `project_id` and `character_id` with the same `_normalize_text()` rules used elsewhere in the service.
Only use repository-backed data that already exists in `app/persistence/story_development.py`.

ordering_rules: Relationship edges should be returned in deterministic edge-id order.
Arc candidates should be returned in deterministic name/arc-id order consistent with repository projection intent.
Arc stage maps should be returned in deterministic arc-id order.

utilized_features: Existing schema conversion helpers already present in `StoryKnowledgeService`
Existing normalization and not-found validation patterns in `StoryKnowledgeService`
expected_outcomes: `hasattr(StoryKnowledgeService, 'list_relationship_edges_for_character')`, `hasattr(..., 'list_arc_candidates')`, and `hasattr(..., 'list_arc_stage_maps')` all become true through concrete method implementations.
Each new method returns schema objects, not raw repository records.
The methods introduce no write behavior, no schema changes, and no new persistence logic.
No existing comparison, selection, or stage-map update behavior changes outside the added read/list surface.

purpose: Harden `FoundationService` input coercion so invalid or incomplete mappings fail through `FoundationValidationError` instead of leaking raw `TypeError`/`KeyError` from `FoundationProfileInput.from_mapping()` or `FoundationProfilePatch.from_mapping()`. Keep the persisted foundation shape unchanged; do not add new foundation fields or extend repository storage in this task.

definitions: Patch fields: any non-empty subset of the existing persisted foundation fields only.
failure_contract: Missing required keys or non-string values must produce `FoundationValidationError` with a deterministic message suitable for router 400 handling.
Patch coercion must not expose raw Python exceptions to callers.

expected_outcomes: Calling `create_foundation_revision()` with an incomplete mapping no longer raises raw `TypeError` or `KeyError`.
Calling `update_foundation_revision()` with an invalid patch no longer leaks raw coercion exceptions.
Valid create/update behavior and revision persistence stay unchanged.
No new foundation fields, repository columns, or response-schema fields are added.
